Among valid disclosures, intc_2024_7_D026 (Network and Edge) discusses moving networks to software infrastructure with AI-enabled compute/connectivity solutions for the edge, and intc_2024_7_D028 (Network and Edge) details the development of high-performance AI-enabled compute platforms and edge-optimized AI-enabled platforms based on Xeon/Core/Atom silicon. Both cover the same specific subject matter of network/edge solutions leveraging AI and silicon portfolios, whereas other candidates like D024 focus on the strategic transformation of fixed-function hardware to general-purpose compute rather than the specific solution deployment aspect described in the anchor.

comparisons.peer_topic: Adaptive Computing and Embedded Systems Portfolio Expansion
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD expanded its adaptive computing portfolio with the launch of Versal Series Gen 2 devices, including Versal AI Edge and Prime Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs, which integrate preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing for end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies describe expanding their portfolios to deliver AI-enabled platforms for edge computing applications. Intel focuses on on-premises edge solutions using its Xeon, Core, and Atom processors to help customers process data faster at the edge across industries like retail and healthcare. AMD similarly expanded its adaptive computing portfolio with Versal Series Gen 2 devices (Versal AI Edge and Prime Series) that integrate preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing for end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems. While Intel emphasizes the partnership model and broad silicon portfolio for edge-optimized platforms, AMD highlights the integration of processing stages into a single device for embedded systems.

sentences.text: On-Premises Edge: More than just providing silicon, we partner with companies to design and deliver solutions to help a wide range of customers transform their businesses and take advantage of the rapidly increasing number of connected and intelligent devices.

We deliver edge-optimized AI-enabled platforms for edge applications based on our Intel Xeon, Intel Core, and Intel Atom® processor portfolio, which reduces operational complexity for our customers and helps our customers create, store, and process data at the edge so they can analyze it faster and act on it sooner.

We expanded our adaptive computing portfolio with differentiated solutions with the launch of the new Versal™ Series Gen 2 devices, including the new Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2 and Versal Prime Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs, which bring preprocessing, AI inference, and postprocessing together in a single device for end-to-end acceleration of AI-driven embedded systems.

comparisons.peer_topic: Global Technology Scope and Product Portfolio
comparisons.peer_summary: Avago is a global technology leader designing semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions, including AI networking, home connectivity, and software for mainframe and cloud platforms, while also offering fibre channel storage area networking products.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address infrastructure solutions that encompass edge and AI capabilities, but they differ in scope and focus. Intel specifically details its 'On-Premises Edge' strategy, partnering with companies to deliver AI-enabled compute platforms using specific processor families (Xeon, Core, Atom) to reduce operational complexity for customers. Avago describes itself broadly as a global technology leader supplying semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions, including AI networking and software for edge, mobile, and cloud platforms. Avago's disclosure is a high-level overview of its diverse product portfolio and software capabilities, whereas Intel's disclosure is a specific operational update on its edge computing business model and technology stack.

sentences.text: We deliver edge-optimized AI-enabled platforms for edge applications based on our Intel Xeon, Intel Core, and Intel Atom® processor portfolio, which reduces operational complexity for our customers and helps our customers create, store, and process data at the edge so they can analyze it faster and act on it sooner.
We are a global technology leader that designs, develops and supplies a broad range of semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions.

Our infrastructure software solutions help enterprises simplify their information technology environments so they can increase business velocity and flexibility, and enable customers to plan, develop, deliver, automate, manage and secure applications across mainframe, distributed, edge, mobile, and private and hybrid cloud platforms.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center AI Inference Platforms and Cloud Services
comparisons.peer_summary: The company launched AI inference platforms combining software with Ada, Hopper, and Grace Hopper processors for generative AI and LLMs. It also introduced NVIDIA DGX Cloud and AI Foundations to help businesses create and operate custom large language models.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA describe the launch of specialized hardware platforms optimized for AI workloads. Intel highlights its 'edge-optimized AI-enabled platforms' based on Xeon, Core, and Atom processors designed to help customers process data faster at the edge. NVIDIA describes launching 'AI inference platforms' that combine its full-stack inference software with processors like Ada, Hopper, and Grace Hopper, optimized for generative AI and LLMs. Both companies are positioning their processor architectures to accelerate AI adoption, with Intel focusing on edge computing use cases and NVIDIA focusing on data center inference and generative AI models.

sentences.text: We deliver edge-optimized AI-enabled platforms for edge applications based on our Intel Xeon, Intel Core, and Intel Atom® processor portfolio, which reduces operational complexity for our customers and helps our customers create, store, and process data at the edge so they can analyze it faster and act on it sooner.

In Data Center, we launched AI inference platforms that combine our full-stack inference software with NVIDIA Ada, NVIDIA Hopper and NVIDIA Grace Hopper processors optimized for generative AI, LLMs and other AI workloads.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm believes that 5G, combined with high-performance computing and on-device AI, will drive adoption in automotive and IoT sectors, and that maintaining leadership in 5G technology development, standardization, and IP licensing is critical for long-term business sustainability.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm discuss the convergence of AI and computing technologies for specific industry applications, though their focus areas differ. Intel describes developing 'on-premises edge' solutions using AI-enabled compute platforms for industries like retail and healthcare to process data at the edge. Qualcomm discusses the belief that '5G combined with high-performance, low-power computing and on-device artificial intelligence' will drive adoption in automotive and IoT sectors. Both identify edge/IoT-like environments (retail/healthcare edge vs. automotive/IoT) as key growth areas for their respective AI and computing technologies, but Intel's disclosure is operational (product delivery), while Qualcomm's is strategic (market adoption drivers).

sentences.text: We develop high-performance, AI-enabled compute platforms that solve for technology and business use cases that scale across several industries, such as retail, education, manufacturing, energy, healthcare, and medical.

We deliver edge-optimized AI-enabled platforms for edge applications based on our Intel Xeon, Intel Core, and Intel Atom® processor portfolio, which reduces operational complexity for our customers and helps our customers create, store, and process data at the edge so they can analyze it faster and act on it sooner.

We believe that 5G combined with high-performance, low-power computing and on-device artificial intelligence will continue to drive adoption of certain technologies that are already commonly used in smartphones by industries and applications beyond mobile handsets, such as automotive and IoT.
